_comment: Firmware below the OS, by the name the 'firmware' source reports: the BIOS/UEFI vendor string, or intel-me / amd-psp / intel-microcode / amd-microcode. Only used by that source. Unlisted BIOS vendors count as nonfree.

entries.name: intel-me
entries.description: Intel Management Engine: a separate computer in the chipset with its own OS, full memory access and network access, running whenever the machine has power. This scan can't tell whether me_cleaner or the HAP bit disabled it

entries.name: amd-psp
entries.description: AMD Platform Security Processor: an ARM core inside the CPU running signed AMD firmware before and beneath the OS

entries.name: intel-microcode
entries.description: CPU microcode; Intel ships it and its updates only as signed binaries

entries.name: amd-microcode
entries.description: CPU microcode; AMD ships it and its updates only as signed binaries

entries.name: coreboot
entries.description: coreboot is free, but most boards also run Intel FSP/ME or AMD AGESA blobs. Libreboot and Canoeboot builds report themselves as coreboot too; mark yours free with --blacklist

entries.name: canoeboot
entries.description: Canoeboot boot firmware (fully free Libreboot fork)

entries.name: seabios
entries.description: SeaBIOS, the default BIOS of QEMU/KVM virtual machines (LGPL-3.0)

entries.name: edk ii
entries.description: EDK II / OVMF UEFI firmware, used by QEMU/KVM virtual machines (BSD-2-Clause-Patent)
